terms.title: EUR-Lex legal notice (disclaimer and copyright notice)

licence.name: EUR-Lex legal notice; consolidated texts under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International

records.attribution_line: EU legislation from EUR-Lex (eur-lex.europa.eu). © European Union, 1998–2026. Consolidated texts are reused under CC BY 4.0. Extract only. Only the Official Journal of the European Union is authentic.
status_lines: Only European Union documents published in the Official Journal of the European Union are deemed authentic.
Extract only, where a single article or a capped passage is shown.
conditions: Documents with special conditions are title and link only: CELEX 32023R1803 and 32008R1126 (international accounting standards), every consolidated version of them, and any regulation whose title says it adopts or amends international accounting standards.
Third-party works inside a document, and content showing identifiable private individuals, may need their own permission.
not_covered: The EUR-Lex logo, which needs the prior consent of the Publications Office
Logos, names, trademarks, patents and registered designs
records.evidence: PDF of the legal notice page saved by the reader on 20 November 2026. Its filing location is tracked on TEC-746.
records.notes: The reader saved and supplied the page; an AI assistant working for the reader read it in full the same day. The notice says the legal documents published in EUR-Lex can be reused for commercial or non-commercial purposes unless otherwise specified, that the consolidated texts are licensed under CC BY 4.0 (acknowledge the source and indicate changes), and that EUR-Lex metadata is CC0. It sets no condition on linking and has no separate term on automated analysis. Regulation (EU) 2023/1803 says in recital 14 that the IFRS Foundation owns the copyright in the standards; Regulation (EC) No 1126/2008 says "Reproduction allowed within the European Economic Area". The eur-lex.europa.eu website returns an empty response to automated requests; the Publications Office endpoints do not. The attribution line and the exclusion rule were approved by the owner on 20 November 2026.

terms.title: EUR-Lex legal notice (disclaimer and copyright notice)

licence.name: EUR-Lex legal notice; reuse policy based on Commission Decision 2011/833/EU

status_lines: Only European Union documents published in the Official Journal of the European Union are deemed authentic.
For case law, only the versions published in the European Court Reports are deemed official sources.
not_covered: The EUR-Lex logo, which needs the prior consent of the Publications Office
Logos, names, trademarks, patents and registered designs
records.evidence: PDF of the legal notice page saved by the reader on 20 November 2026. Its filing location is tracked on TEC-746.
records.notes: The reader saved and supplied the page; an AI assistant working for the reader read it in full the same day. Held at link only. The notice allows commercial and non-commercial reuse of the legal documents published in EUR-Lex unless otherwise specified, but this source covers legislation as adopted and case law, and two things are not settled for those: no attribution line has been approved, and judgments name people, so the data protection check comes first (TEC-761, TEC-763). The CC BY 4.0 wording in the notice is for consolidated texts and summaries, which are recorded under EU/ConsolidatedLegislation.

terms.title: Irish Statute Book, Open Data Initiative
Houses of the Oireachtas, copyright and re-use

licence.name: Oireachtas (Public Sector Information – Open Data) Licence, incorporating Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International

records.attribution_line: Irish legislation from the electronic Irish Statute Book (irishstatutebook.ie), produced by the Office of the Attorney General. © Houses of the Oireachtas. Reused under the Oireachtas (Public Sector Information – Open Data) Licence, which incorporates CC BY 4.0. Extract only. Publication does not mean a provision is in force; see the Irish Statute Book disclaimer.
status_lines: As enacted or as made, not revised.
Publication of legislation on the Irish Statute Book does not indicate that a provision was, or is currently, in force.
Extract only, where a single section or a capped passage is shown.
not_covered: Logos, crests and insignia, such as the official harp and other State emblems of Ireland
Rights of third persons that the licensor is not authorised to license
Documents whose re-use is restricted to protect a person's personal data
Broadcast proceedings, which have their own licence
records.evidence: PDF of the licence dated 27 March 2016, supplied by the reader on 20 November 2026. Its filing location is tracked on TEC-746.
records.notes: The Statute Book's open data page says re-use of the data on the site is subject to the Oireachtas (Open Data) PSI Licence. Clause 3.2 requires the re-user to identify the Houses of the Oireachtas as creator, keep the copyright notice, keep a reference to the licence and keep any disclaimer notice. An Act read as XML and as HTML and a statutory instrument read as HTML carried no copyright notice of their own. The owner decided on 20 November 2026 that statutory instruments are credited to the Houses of the Oireachtas, as Acts are, and approved the attribution line. The reader supplied and confirmed the licence and the copyright and re-use wording; the open data and disclaimer pages were retrieved and read by an AI assistant working for the reader on the same day. legal-sources labels this source "Irish Open Government Licence", which is not what the site says.
